facts.text: Mackinaw City hosts Colonial Michilimackinac, a National Historic Landmark accredited by the American Association of Museums.
The fort that now sits in Mackinaw City was preserved as an open‑air historical museum and is a National Historic Landmark.
In 1761 the French ceded Fort Michilimackinac in Mackinaw City to the British, who abandoned it in 1781 for Fort Mackinac on the island.
The name Mackinaw comes from Ojibwe mishinii‑makinaang, meaning “at the place of many snapping turtles,” reflecting the region’s turtle‑shaped straits.
Mackinaw City sits at the southern end of the Mackinac Bridge, where Lake Huron and Lake Michigan meet.
June 27–28, 2026, Mackinaw City hosts an Arts & Crafts Show at historic Conkling Heritage Park, featuring handcrafted wares.
